title: Multivalued Dependency (MVD) in DBMS - GeeksforGeeks
content:
A Multivalued Dependency (MVD) occurs when one attribute determines multiple independent values of another attribute. It is used when two or more attributes have independent sets of values associated with the same attribute.

  • MVD is represented using the →→ symbol.
  • It commonly occurs when multiple values of two attributes are independent of each other.

Example

Consider a relation where a student can have multiple projects and multiple hobbies:

Student_IDProjectHobby
1MSReading
1OracleMusic
1MSMusic
1OracleReading

Here, the projects and hobbies are independent of each other for Student_ID = 1. Each project can be associated with each hobby, giving all possible combinations.

Therefore:

Student_ID →→ Project

This indicates that Student_ID determines multiple Project values independently of Hobby.

Conditions for MVD

An attribute a is said to multivalued determine another attribute b, written as a →→ b, if for every pair of tuples t1 and t2 in a relation r(R) having the same value of a, there must exist tuples t3 and t4 in r such that:

t1[a] = t2[a] = t3[a] = t4[a]

t1[b] = t3[b]

t2[b] = t4[b]

t1[c] = t4[c]

t2[c] = t3[c]

where c represents the remaining attributes of the relation other than a and b.

For the given NAME, PROJECT, and HOBBY relation:

Condition 1

t1[NAME] = t2[NAME] = t3[NAME] = t4[NAME] = Geeks

The values of NAME are the same, so Condition 1 is satisfied.

Condition 2

t1[PROJECT] = t3[PROJECT] = MS
t2[PROJECT] = t4[PROJECT] = Oracle

The project values are preserved between the corresponding tuples, so Condition 2 is satisfied.

Condition 3

t1[HOBBY] = t4[HOBBY] = Reading
t2[HOBBY] = t3[HOBBY] = Music

The remaining attribute values are exchanged as required, so Condition 3 is satisfied.

Since all three conditions are satisfied:

NAME →→ PROJECT

Similarly:

NAME →→ HOBBY

Therefore, the given relation contains multivalued dependencies.

Advantages

  • Reduces Redundancy: Separating independent multivalued attributes can reduce repeated combinations of data.
  • Better Data Organization: Independent sets of values can be stored separately, making the database structure clearer.
  • Improves Consistency: Changes to one set of values do not require unnecessary changes to another.

Disadvantages

  • More Tables: Decomposing a relation to handle MVDs can increase the number of tables.
  • More Joins: Retrieving related information may require joins between the decomposed tables.
  • Complex Design: Identifying independent multivalued relationships correctly can make database design more involved.
